question: Magnetic field lines at north pole of a magnet are:
solution:
The correct answer is **lines emerging from the pole.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines**

 
 
• **​**The **magnet or moving electric charges** create a field known as the magnetic field. The region within which the force of magnetism operates around a magnetic substance or **moving electric charge** is known as the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/175de06bdbbf9738b8d7f0ca3ec60fb626e04dc1856f10ee60f1f51e2c9953fe.png] 
 
• Magnetic field lines are used to represent magnetic fields. It is a visual tool used to visualize the **magnetic field's direction and strength**.
 
• A **compass needle **can be used to draw lines in a magnetic field. Place the compass needle on a piece of paper close to the magnet.
 
• Mark the direction that the compass needle is pointing in after you have checked it.
 
• Mark the directions by moving the compass needle to **various positions.** The lines of the magnetic field can be seen by joining the points.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Magnetic Field Lines**

 
 
• The magnetic field's direction can be determined by** tangenting** the lines of the field.
 
• The **field strength **is directly proportional to the **density or closeness** of the field lines.
 
• Lines in the magnetic field appear to **start** at the **north pole** and merge or **end at** the **south pole.**
 
• The magnetic field lines that run** inside the magnet **run from the **south pole to the north pole**.
 
• Lines of the magnetic field **never cross each other.**
 
• A **closed loop** is formed by magnetic field lines.
 
• At any point on the field, field lines have **magnitude** as well as **direction**. Consequently, a vector is used to represent magnetic field lines.
 
• They indicate the magnetic field's direction.
 
• Because the field lines are **denser near the poles**, the magnetic field is **stronger at the poles**.
